groups.title: NSF project: Future Proofing for Age-Related Changing Cognitive Abilities Using Smart Objects as Assistive Technologies
bullets: Built an AI agent (Python, Flask, Gemini API, Gmail and Google Calendar APIs) that connects to a user's email and calendar to infer their plans, routines, relationships, and commitments, grouping each inference by topic with its source, answering voice and text questions, and adapting its inferences to the rules and boundaries users set in plain language.

Led co-design sessions with 6 people living with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia using the agent as a design probe: walked participants through a demo built on a synthetic persona dataset, then guided them in authoring their own rules for what the agent may read, what it may infer, and when it should share, using Data Sources, Inferences, and Timing card decks; followed up with reflection interviews.

Conducted a 7-participant, 14-session co-design study with people living with MCI or dementia: developed the study protocol, designed Figma design cards with collaborators as probes, and ran one-on-one remote sessions (Zoom, FigJam) progressing from a shared leaving-home use case to each participant's own meaningful use case.

Analyzed co-design data with reflexive thematic analysis: independently coded and memoed 8 of 14 transcripts, then refined and finalized themes with the research team, testing counterexamples and verifying quotes.

Conducted semi-structured interviews with people living with MCI or dementia on everyday technology use (three per participant, paired with a two-week diary study), tailoring follow-up probes and grounding post-diary interviews in each participant's entries.

Proposed an adaptive systems framework of four user-configurable modules (sensing, inference, assistance authority, output delivery), presented as a lead-author CSCW 2026 poster, and built the Raspberry Pi leaving-home reminder system that implements it (Gemini API, dlib face recognition, Google Calendar, weather data, Flask configuration app).

groups.title: Research Assistant
bullets: Analyzed older adults' self-presentation on TikTok, combining engagement data for 15,000+ videos from 23 creators with a team-coded set of 1,227 videos from 11 creators.
Mentored four undergraduate and graduate students across research and prototyping projects, from study procedures and qualitative analysis to building working prototypes.
Publications: lead-author poster, CSCW 2026; co-author, ASSETS 2026 full paper (Honorable Mention Award).

summary: Built and shipped web features for an early-stage startup, working with it through an Arizona State University program.
bullets: Turned Figma designs into responsive web applications in React and TypeScript, iterating with the design team from handoff to release.
Designed and integrated RESTful APIs to move data between user-facing features and the backend.
Built a HubSpot chatbot that automated customer engagement, cutting manual intervention by 40%.
Standardized 550+ templates with global variables, so one change updates everywhere and manual updates dropped by 80%.

summary: Radar perception and object tracking for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), the technology behind features like adaptive cruise control.
bullets: Implemented C++ multi-object tracking with a Kalman Filter, Interacting Multiple Model (IMM), and Probabilistic Data Association Filter (PDAF), improving vehicle tracking accuracy by 10%.
Improved ADAS object classification by 5% through MATLAB-based feature extraction and radar data analysis.
Identified and resolved a critical bug in which a truck was classified as two separate cars, raising classification accuracy by 15%.
Labeled and validated 5,000+ video frames against radar sensor outputs.
